question: Why are the testes located outside the main body cavity in the scrotum?

options.A: To produce testosterone for secondary sex traits
options.B: To store mature sperm cells before ejaculation
options.C: To keep the testes cooler than core body temperature
options.D: To secrete fluid that forms the bulk of semen

explanation: You've got this! Sperm production works best at a slightly lower temperature than our normal body heat. That is why nature designed the scrotum to hang outside the body to keep the testes nice and cool. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T1#GNS311_U1_T1_h1)

question: Which part of the penis directly wraps around and surrounds the urethra?
explanation: Great job thinking through the anatomy! The corpus spongiosum is the single column of spongy tissue that houses and protects the urethra as it runs down to the tip. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T1#GNS311_U1_T1_h1)

question: Where exactly inside the testes are sperm cells made?
explanation: Think of the seminiferous tubules as tiny, packed-together factories inside the testes where germ cells constantly grow and transform into brand new sperm! [learn more](GNS311_U1_T1#GNS311_U1_T1_h2)

question: What is the main job of the Leydig cells found in the testes?

options.A: Protecting developing germ cells from immune attack
options.B: Providing nutritional support to immature spermatids
options.C: Transporting mature sperm out of the lobules
options.D: Producing and secreting the hormone testosterone

explanation: You're doing great! Leydig cells hang out right between the sperm-producing tubes and are responsible for pumping out testosterone, the key male hormone. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T1#GNS311_U1_T1_h2)

question: What happens to sperm when they hang out in the epididymis?

options.A: To allow sperm to mature and gain swimming ability
options.B: To cool down the testes during physical exertion
options.C: To filter out abnormal sperm cells using white blood cells
options.D: To add fructose-rich fluid to the seminal mixture

explanation: Think of the epididymis as a training ground! Newly made sperm aren't ready to swim yet; they spend time here resting, maturing, and learning how to swim. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T1#GNS311_U1_T1_h3)

question: How do sperm travel upward through the long vas deferens during ejaculation?

options.A: By beating their flagella very rapidly
options.B: By suction created by the prostate gland
options.D: By gravity pulling them down into the urethra

explanation: Just like food moves down your gut, the walls of the vas deferens use wave-like muscle squeezes (peristalsis) to push sperm smoothly along their journey. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T1#GNS311_U1_T1_h3)

question: Which male reproductive gland adds the most fluid volume to semen?
explanation: Spot on! The seminal vesicles are generous contributors, providing about 60% of semen fluid along with sugary fructose to give the sperm energy. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T1#GNS311_U1_T1_h4)

question: Why do the bulbourethral glands release a clear mucus right before ejaculation?

options.A: To neutralize any leftover acid from urine in the urethra
options.B: To provide the main energy source for sperm motility
options.C: To activate sperm flagella for faster swimming
options.D: To cause the semen to clot firmly inside the vagina

explanation: Urine is quite acidic and can harm delicate sperm. This clever little mucus fluid cleanses the urethra path first so the sperm can pass safely! [learn more](GNS311_U1_T1#GNS311_U1_T1_h4)

question: Which hormone signals the Leydig cells in the testes to make testosterone?
explanation: You've got this! Luteinizing hormone (LH) travels from the brain's pituitary gland down to the testes, giving the green light for testosterone production. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T1#GNS311_U1_T1_h5)

question: How would you explain a negative feedback loop of hormones to a curious patient?

options.A: It allows the brain to control your heart rate and breathing rate simultaneously.
options.B: It prevents the testes from ever changing in size throughout your lifetime.
options.C: It stops the body from producing too much testosterone when levels are already high.
options.D: It ensures that the pituitary gland stops working completely during physical rest.

explanation: Think of it like an air conditioner thermostat! When hormone levels get high enough, a signal goes back to the brain to slow things down so the body doesn't overproduce. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T1#GNS311_U1_T1_h5)
